record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: Let a polyomino be a strongly connected union of axis-aligned unit squares on the square lattice. An isohedral tiling is a tiling of the plane by congruent copies of the polyomino such that any two copies are related by a symmetry of the tiling. If n is the number of unit-length edges on the boundary of the polyomino, is there an O(n)-time algorithm that decides whether the polyomino admits an isohedral tiling?

evidence.quote: Definitions. A polyomino is a subset of R2 formed by a strongly connected union of axis-aligned unit squares centered at locations on the square lattice Z2.
If a tiling T has the property that for all Ti, Tj∈ T , there exists a symmetry of T mapping Ti to Tj, then T is isohedral; otherwise the tiling is non-isohedral

The fastest known algorithm for testing these criteria runs in O(n log2 n) time [27], where n is the number of unit-length edges along the boundary of the polyomino. Is a faster algorithm possible? Open Problem 1 (Open Problem 2 of [27]) Is there an O(n)-time algorithm for determining whether a polyomino has an isohedral tiling?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a polyomino to be a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ formed by a strongly connected (edge-connected) union of axis-aligned closed unit squares centered at points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. A tiling of the plane by congruent copies $\{T_i\}$ of such a polyomino $P$ is called isohedral if for every pair of tiles $T_i, T_j$ there is a symmetry of the tiling (an isometry of $\mathbb{R}^2$ preserving the entire tiling) that maps $T_i$ to $T_j$. Let $n$ denote the number of unit-length edges on the boundary of $P$.

Is there an algorithm that, given $P$ specified by its boundary word of length $n$, decides in $O(n)$ time whether $P$ admits an isohedral tiling of the plane?
artifact.status_search_result: The best known algorithm for deciding whether a polyomino admits an isohedral tiling runs in O(n log² n) time (Langerman–Winslow, SoCG 2016), improving Keating–Vince's earlier polynomial-time algorithm. No O(n)-time algorithm appears in the literature, and the question of whether linear-time recognition is achievable remains posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A Quasilinear-Time Algorithm for Tiling the Plane Isohedrally with a Polyomino
status_evidence.snippet: O(n log^2 n)-time algorithm for deciding if a polyomino with n edges can tile the plane isohedrally.
status_evidence.claim: Current best known complexity is O(n log^2 n), not O(n).

status_evidence.title: A Quasilinear-Time Algorithm for Tiling the Plane Isohedrally with a Polyomino (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves Keating–Vince O(n^18); leaves open whether a linear-time algorithm exists.
status_evidence.claim: Linear-time isohedral tiling recognition remains open.
